author: Karl Rock
description:
I found a Hindu temple island in Pakistan with nine temples hidden on it.

Sadhu Bela sits in the middle of the Indus River near Sukkur, Sindh, and has been an important Hindu pilgrimage site for generations. Getting there meant crossing the river by boat, and exploring this incredible, little-known piece of Hindu heritage in Pakistan was an experience I’ll never forget.

More about Sadhu Bela:

Sadhu Bela, also known as Sadh Belo, is a Hindu temple complex built on an island in the Indus River near Sukkur, Sindh. The island was once known as Menak Parbat, a forested and largely uninhabited place. In 1823, an Udasi ascetic named Baba Bankhandi Maharaj settled here and established a spiritual centre. The name Sadhu Bela is generally understood to mean “woods of the sage.”
